From parity checks to fault-tolerant machinesReview · 0 due

Module 4 · 150-190 minutes

Measuring a surface code: circuits, detectors and Google's memory experiments

What does a measurement circuit do to the faults it encounters, and how does its record become a measured logical error rate?

Assumes: Module 1: syndrome differences, logical error per round and suppression ratios · Module 2: Clifford Pauli propagation, stabilizer measurement and Pauli frames · Module 3: canonical rotated patch checks, boundaries and logical directions · Circuit QED background: weakly anharmonic levels and coherent two-level evolution

Requires: The toric and surface codes · Enables: Decoding and thresholds

By the end, you can
  • Derive the data Pauli measured by a CNOT or CZ extraction circuit.
  • Propagate an ancilla fault and choose a compatible schedule with hook pairs perpendicular to the same-type logical direction.
  • Construct bulk and boundary detectors and map an elementary fault to its detector and logical signatures.
  • Specify the fault locations and probability convention in a noise model and identify missing correlations.
  • Calculate phase and leakage in a reduced CZ model and connect gate, idle, reset and leakage errors to a QEC cycle.
  • Extract error per cycle from logical contrast decay and interpret a decoder-specific suppression ratio and error budget.
  1. 4.1 · Which operator does this circuit measure?
  2. 4.2 · Hook errors and schedules
  3. 4.3 · Detectors, detection events and the detector error model
  4. 4.4 · Noise models: what is allowed to fail?
  5. 4.5 · Leakage, bursts and the floor
  6. 4.6 · The device behind the circuit
  7. 4.7 · Sycamore to Willow
  8. 4.8 · Reconstruct and transfer

We will follow one circuit fault from its physical origin to the measurement record and the decoded logical outcome. The circuits reuse Module 3's rotated patch. A natural break comes after the noise models. Syndrome and detector values are bits; error rates carry their operation or round denominator; angular frequencies are in radians per unit time, and the device plots label ordinary frequencies in MHz.

A measure qubit starts in zero, receives a Hadamard, touches four data qubits through CZ gates, receives another Hadamard, and is measured. The circuit is labeled “X check.” Which property of the data does its result actually reveal?

After fixing that label, let the measure qubit suffer a fault halfway through the sequence. Can a circuit that measures the right property still damage the memory it is checking?

§

4.1 · Which operator does this circuit measure?

Hadamards on the measure qubit alone make the CZ circuit measure Z1Z2Z4Z5Z_1Z_2Z_4Z_5Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​. Hadamards on those data qubits before and after the interaction make it an X check. We can see why by following the final measured Pauli backward through the gates.

The measure qubit, or ancilla, is a temporary parity register, labeled A. The four data corners are NW, NE, SW and SE, with north at the top of the page. For check X-a they are qubits 1,2,4,51,2,4,51,2,4,5 in that order. The measured observable is the data property mapped into A's readout. Here the computational basis means the ZZZ eigenbasis, with ∣0⟩|0\rangle∣0⟩ assigned eigenvalue +1+1+1.

In the Z circuit, each data bit controls whether A flips. The final A value records their parity. In the X circuit, A controls a product of data X operations. Interference between its control branches reveals the eigenvalue of that product. These are the extraction directions used by Fowler and by Tomita and Svore Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation, PDF p. 5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.86.032324 Low-distance Surface Codes under Realistic Quantum Noise, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062320.

Parity extraction preserves superpositions within each parity sector.

To trace gates systematically, use Module 2's Pauli bits: P∝XxZzP\propto X^xZ^zP∝XxZz. A CNOT has control c and target t. Its X part copies forward and its Z part copies backward:

Derivation · Translate the Pauli conjugations into bits

Track each basis Pauli separately, then multiply its images. The CNOT images are Xc↦XcXtX_c\mapsto X_cX_tXc​↦Xc​Xt​, Zc↦ZcZ_c\mapsto Z_cZc​↦Zc​, Xt↦XtX_t\mapsto X_tXt​↦Xt​ and Zt↦ZcZtZ_t\mapsto Z_cZ_tZt​↦Zc​Zt​. For example, the target X exponent becomes xt+xcx_t+x_cxt​+xc​ modulo two because both input X factors contribute there. The control Z exponent becomes zc+ztz_c+z_tzc​+zt​ for the same reason. Hadamard exchanges X and Z. The diagonal CZ matrix diag⁡(1,1,1,−1)\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,-1)diag(1,1,1,−1) obeys

CZXcCZ=XcZt,CZXtCZ=ZcXt,CZZcCZ=Zc,CZZtCZ=Zt.\mathrm{CZ}X_c\mathrm{CZ}=X_cZ_t,\qquad \mathrm{CZ}X_t\mathrm{CZ}=Z_cX_t,\qquad \mathrm{CZ}Z_c\mathrm{CZ}=Z_c,\quad \mathrm{CZ}Z_t\mathrm{CZ}=Z_t.CZXc​CZ=Xc​Zt​,CZXt​CZ=Zc​Xt​,CZZc​CZ=Zc​,CZZt​CZ=Zt​.

Each input X therefore adds a Z on the other wire. Phases require separate tracking: HYH=−YHYH=-YHYH=−Y even though its two bits are unchanged. Pauli support suffices to find anticommuting checks; a signed measured observable also needs that phase.

What does the CZ circuit reveal?

A is reset, receives H, interacts through CZ with qubits 1,2,4,51,2,4,51,2,4,5, receives H, and is measured in Z. What data observable is measured?

The final H exposes XAX_AXA​ in backward propagation. Each CZ appends a data Z. The initial H restores ZAZ_AZA​, whose reset eigenvalue is known. Removing that known factor leaves data Z parity.

Your prediction

CZ changes an ancilla X into ancilla X times data Z. With HDH_DHD​ denoting Hadamards on all participating data qubits,

CZAqXACZAq=XAZq,UCZ†ZAUCZ=ZAZNWZNEZSWZSE,(HDUCZHD)†ZA(HDUCZHD)=ZAXNWXNEXSWXSE.\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CZ}_{Aq}X_A\mathrm{CZ}_{Aq}&=X_AZ_q,\\ U_{\rm CZ}^\dagger Z_AU_{\rm CZ}&=Z_AZ_{\rm NW}Z_{\rm NE}Z_{\rm SW}Z_{\rm SE},\\ (H_DU_{\rm CZ}H_D)^\dagger Z_A(H_DU_{\rm CZ}H_D) &=Z_AX_{\rm NW}X_{\rm NE}X_{\rm SW}X_{\rm SE}. \end{aligned}CZAq​XA​CZAq​UCZ†​ZA​UCZ​(HD​UCZ​HD​)†ZA​(HD​UCZ​HD​)​=XA​Zq​,=ZA​ZNW​ZNE​ZSW​ZSE​,=ZA​XNW​XNE​XSW​XSE​.​
(4.3)
Derivation · Follow the readout through the CZ block

Conjugate in reverse gate order. The final H changes ZAZ_AZA​ to XAX_AXA​. Each CZ attaches its partner's Z and leaves every previously attached Z unchanged. The input H changes the surviving XAX_AXA​ back to ZAZ_AZA​. Its eigenvalue on the reset state is positive. For the repaired circuit, the final data Hadamards commute with the readout ZAZ_AZA​; the input data Hadamards then convert each attached Z to X, using HZH=XHZH=XHZH=X. Both measured operators have positive sign. The data basis gates select the data parity, while the ancilla basis gates expose it to readout.

Audit the label on X-a

For corner order NE, NW, SE, SW, the backward chain is

ZA⟼XA⟼XAZ4⟼XAZ4Z5⟼XAZ1Z4Z5⟼XAZ1Z2Z4Z5⟼ZAZ1Z2Z4Z5.Z_A\longmapsto X_A\longmapsto X_AZ_4\longmapsto X_AZ_4Z_5 \longmapsto X_AZ_1Z_4Z_5\longmapsto X_AZ_1Z_2Z_4Z_5 \longmapsto Z_AZ_1Z_2Z_4Z_5.ZA​⟼XA​⟼XA​Z4​⟼XA​Z4​Z5​⟼XA​Z1​Z4​Z5​⟼XA​Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​⟼ZA​Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​.

The data property is Z1Z2Z4Z5Z_1Z_2Z_4Z_5Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​. Surrounding the block with data Hadamards changes it to the intended X1X2X4X5X_1X_2X_4X_5X1​X2​X4​X5​. Nothing about the label on the circuit enters this calculation.

How can this CZ circuit measure the intended X check?

Your answer

You can now determine the parity a circuit measures without trusting its label. The next question is what happens when the measure qubit itself is faulty.

§

4.2 · Hook errors and schedules

A measure qubit touches several data qubits in one round. A fault on it can therefore spread to more than one data qubit before it is read.

A fault location names a gate, idle, reset or measurement where an elementary error may occur. A hook error is the correlated data support left by one extraction fault. To find that support, propagate the fault forward through the gates that remain. An ancilla X spreads through ancilla-controlled CNOTs; an ancilla Z spreads through CNOTs targeting the ancilla.

Let the check's data order be q1,…,q4q_1,\ldots,q_4q1​,…,q4​. After kkk completed gates, the propagating ancilla Pauli PAP_APA​ leaves

Edata=∏j=k+14Pqj,P=X for X extraction,P=Z for Z extraction.E_{\rm data}=\prod_{j=k+1}^{4}P_{q_j},\qquad P=X\ \text{for X extraction},\quad P=Z\ \text{for Z extraction}.Edata​=j=k+1∏4​Pqj​​,P=X for X extraction,P=Z for Z extraction.
(4.4)
Derivation · Keep the ancilla until its last interaction

Apply the CNOT propagation rule at each remaining interaction. For X extraction the successive errors are

XA⟼XAXqk+1⟼XAXqk+1Xqk+2⟼⋯⟼XA∏j=k+14Xqj.X_A\longmapsto X_AX_{q_{k+1}}\longmapsto X_AX_{q_{k+1}}X_{q_{k+2}}\longmapsto\cdots\longmapsto X_A\prod_{j=k+1}^4X_{q_j}.XA​⟼XA​Xqk+1​​⟼XA​Xqk+1​​Xqk+2​​⟼⋯⟼XA​j=k+1∏4​Xqj​​.

The final ancilla H converts XAX_AXA​ to ZAZ_AZA​, which does not flip its Z readout. For Z extraction, backward copying through each CNOT means ZA↦ZqjZAZ_A\mapsto Z_{q_j}Z_AZA​↦Zqj​​ZA​; there is no final ancilla H. The final data support is the stated tail in either case. Multiplication by the measured check S=∏j=14PqjS=\prod_{j=1}^4P_{q_j}S=∏j=14​Pqj​​ exchanges tail and complement:

EdataS=∏j=1kPqj,wraw=4−k,wmodulo check=min⁡(k,4−k).E_{\rm data}S=\prod_{j=1}^kP_{q_j},\qquad w_{\rm raw}=4-k,\qquad w_{\rm modulo\ check}=\min(k,4-k).Edata​S=j=1∏k​Pqj​​,wraw​=4−k,wmodulo check​=min(k,4−k).

For k=0,1,2,3,4k=0,1,2,3,4k=0,1,2,3,4, raw weights are 4,3,2,1,04,3,2,1,04,3,2,1,0 and reduced weights are 0,1,2,1,00,1,2,1,00,1,2,1,0. The reduction uses a fixed check sector; its eigenvalue changes only an overall sign. The midpoint tail remains a pair. Stabilizer equivalence does not remove the need to examine its direction.

The raw weight counts data qubits touched by the error. The stabilizer-equivalent weight is the smallest support after multiplying by stabilizers. Multiplying this tail by its measured check exchanges it with the already-touched complement. Thus a three-data tail is equivalent to a single-data error, while the midpoint tail remains a pair on this patch.

The same-type logical direction means the direction of the logical Pauli matching the hook's Pauli type. Here Xˉ=X1X4X7\bar X=X_1X_4X_7Xˉ=X1​X4​X7​ is vertical. The horizontal X hook does not advance through two rows of that logical string. This is why the last pair, rather than the first pair touched, determines the useful local orientation Low-distance Surface Codes under Realistic Quantum Noise, PDF pp. 4-5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062320.

A misleading final syndrome

The horizontal hook X4X5X_4X_5X4​X5​ anticommutes with Z-a through qubit 5 and with Z-c through qubit 4. It overlaps Z-b twice, so those two signs cancel. Its flagged checks are Z-a and Z-c.

The vertical pair X1X4X_1X_4X1​X4​ flags only Z-b, the same final syndrome as X7X_7X7​. If a recovery chooses X7X_7X7​, the residual is

(X1X4)X7=X1X4X7=Xˉ.(X_1X_4)X_7=X_1X_4X_7=\bar X.(X1​X4​)X7​=X1​X4​X7​=Xˉ.

One extraction fault has produced two data errors. These comparisons use the final data syndrome; an entire circuit record can contain additional information about when each check encountered the fault.

The Z logical is horizontal: Zˉ=Z1Z2Z3\bar Z=Z_1Z_2Z_3Zˉ=Z1​Z2​Z3​. The preferred Z-a hook Z2Z5Z_2Z_5Z2​Z5​ flags X-b and X-c. The dangerous pair Z5Z6Z_5Z_6Z5​Z6​ flags only X-a, as does Z1Z_1Z1​. Their product obeys Z1Z5Z6=Zˉ (Z2Z3Z5Z6)Z_1Z_5Z_6=\bar Z\,(Z_2Z_3Z_5Z_6)Z1​Z5​Z6​=Zˉ(Z2​Z3​Z5​Z6​). The stabilizer factor cannot repair its logical action.

Does a neighboring check absorb the hook?

Why does the horizontal X hook preserve the intended local orientation?

Your answer

A gate layer groups operations that run simultaneously on disjoint wires. A schedule assigns every interaction to a layer. Good hook directions must fit a complete schedule: two checks cannot use the same data qubit at once. On their shared data, overlapping X and Z checks must also have compatible relative ordering so their ancillas do not measure an unwanted joint property Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation, PDF pp. 5-6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.86.032324.

Use X order NE, NW, SE, SW and Z order NE, SE, NW, SW on our fixed patch:

Check Layer 1 Layer 2 Layer 3 Layer 4
X-a 2 1 5 4
X-b 6 5 9 8
X-c idle idle 3 2
X-d 8 7 idle idle
Z-a 3 6 2 5
Z-b 5 8 4 7
Z-c 1 4 idle idle
Z-d idle idle 6 9

Each layer has six disjoint CNOTs, for 24 per round. Reset every ancilla, apply H to the X ancillas, run the four layers, apply H to the X ancillas again, then measure all ancillas in Z. Wires without an operation idle during that layer. Boundary slots matter: X-c uses SW and SE; X-d uses NW and NE; Z-c uses NE and SE; Z-d uses NW and SW.

Google's physical circuit instead uses CZ, interleaved Hadamards and an echo pulse, with locally equivalent ZXXZ checks Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 25 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. Its pulse sequence needs its own fault analysis.

Circuit distance counts the fewest allowed elementary faults that leave no predictable measurement comparison violated but change the logical outcome. This differs from Pauli distance, which counts data support, and from the smaller fault count at which a particular decoder might choose the wrong explanation. For this CNOT schedule, three rounds with product preparation and matching-basis destructive readout have circuit distance three in both X and Z memories. The fault set allows every nonidentity Pauli after a gate or idle, preparation/reset flips and report flips. No allowed single fault or pair is undetected and logically nontrivial. Three final readout errors across a transverse logical support provide a witness. We will express this test with detector signatures in §4.3.

The check-circuit lab isolates one bulk check. basis selects X-a or Z-a; gate selects CNOT or CZ; data_h surrounds a CZ block with data Hadamards. order selects its corner sequence. fault is the Pauli on the physical ancilla wire, inserted after k completed interactions. step changes the displayed history, not the final result. The data may start in any state; reset and readout are ideal. The readouts distinguish the measured operator, final data error, raw and stabilizer-equivalent weight, and ancilla readout flip. The patch view supplies geometry, without simulating neighboring checks.

Which gates remain?

X-a uses NE, NW, SE, SW. An XAX_AXA​ fault occurs after two CNOTs. Which data support remains?

Only the remaining gates copy the ancilla X. They touch data 5 and then 4, leaving X4X5X_4X_5X4​X5​.

Held fixed
  • The canonical distance-three patch has data qubits 1 through 9 in row-major order. X-a acts on 1, 2, 4, 5; Z-a acts on 2, 3, 5, 6. Logical X runs vertically on 1, 4, 7; logical Z runs horizontally on 1, 2, 3.
  • Ancilla reset and final Z measurement are ideal. The selected fault is one ancilla Pauli.
  • CNOT extraction of X uses ancilla control and H on the ancilla before and after the sequence. CNOT extraction of Z uses data controls and no H gates.
  • CZ extraction always has H on the ancilla before and after the sequence. Enabling data H adds H on all four data wires before the first CZ and after the last CZ, so the actual data observable changes from Z to X.
Initial conditions
The ancilla starts in ∣0⟩\lvert0\rangle∣0⟩; the data state is arbitrary. Follow the final ancilla Z observable backward to identify the measured data operator. Follow the selected fault forward from its insertion.
Boundary conditions
Only one four-data check is simulated. The surrounding distance-three patch supplies the end-of-circuit syndrome and logical directions; neighboring extraction circuits are absent.
Measured operator and Pauli history
Full initial/final basis gates; backward measured observable and forward physical fault history; actual operator, intended operator, match yes/no, ancilla readout-flip bit. Horizontal: Gate checkpoint (blocks). Vertical: Wire (qubit labels).
Final data error on the canonical patch
Data Pauli support, raw and modulo-measured-check weights, orientation relative to same-type logical. Compare supports only when pure homogeneous X or Z and measured operator equals the intended check; otherwise say not applicable. Horizontal: Column (lattice spacings). Vertical: Row downward (lattice spacings).
Data-error weight versus fault time
Raw weight and weight reduced modulo the measured check for fault times k = 0 through 4, holding the circuit, order, intended basis and physical ancilla fault fixed. Markers show the selected k. The reduced curve is absent when the model reports that reduction is not applicable; this absence does not mean zero weight. Horizontal: Completed entangling gates at fault insertion (gates). Vertical: Final data-error weight (data qubits).

Method: Track signed Pauli operators on the ancilla and four data wires with integer binary X and Z components and a phase. Conjugate the measured ancilla Z backward through every gate, then take its expectation in the reset ancilla. An ancilla I or Z factor leaves a deterministic data Pauli; X or Y would not. Independently conjugate the inserted fault through the remaining gates. Its final ancilla X component gives the readout-flip bit. Evaluate the final data syndrome against all eight patch checks. For a matching intended measurement and homogeneous same-type error, minimize weight over the error and its product with the measured check only. Compare a two-qubit row or column with the same-type logical direction.

Tolerances: Pauli phases, supports, syndromes and weights use exact integer arithmetic. Independent 32-dimensional matrix checks compare every entry within 1e-12. Integer row and column labels determine orientation.

Display conventions

  • Time runs left to right in the circuit; patch rows increase downward. Data are rings, X checks filled squares and Z checks hollow squares. X error markers are solid, Z markers dashed and Y markers split.
  • The displayed checkpoint counts entangling gates only. Checkpoint 0 follows all input H gates; checkpoint 4 precedes all output H gates. Both H layers and every individual gate appear in the history.
  • The pair orientation describes local geometry. It does not establish that a concurrent schedule is safe.
  • The syndrome is the final data error anticommutation pattern with the eight canonical checks, not a repeated-round detector record.
  • The weight plot uses a solid raw-weight line and a dashed modulo-check line. Lines connect five discrete insertion times; no intermediate fault times are simulated. Both weights include the output Hadamards and remain independent of the displayed gate-history checkpoint.

Commit your prediction above to start the lab — or skip.

Model limits

No circuit noise distribution or decoder is simulated.

One-check correctness and pair orientation do not certify concurrent extraction, boundary handling or circuit distance.

CZ and CNOT faults with the same physical letter need not be the same fault under basis compilation.

The model is limited to five simulated wires, four entangling gates and three corner orders. It does not search a larger circuit or infer a decoder correction.

Tangent: saving measure qubits costs time

Optional. Reusing a measure qubit can reduce the hardware count. It must finish one check, be reset and then collect the next. Tomita and Svore compare such reuse with a dedicated ancilla for each check Low-distance Surface Codes under Realistic Quantum Noise, PDF p. 3 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062320. The saved hardware changes circuit depth and idle exposure. Return to detector records.

You can now trace a hook and judge its direction on the patch. To decide whether a complete fault history is dangerous, we need the record that the decoder actually sees.

4.3 · Detectors, detection events and the detector error model

The decoder needs to know which measurement relationships have failed. A detector tests a relationship that would have a predictable value if the circuit were noiseless.

The measurement record is the ordered list of measured bits mjm_jmj​. A detector specifies a set RaR_aRa​ of those bits whose parity has a deterministic reference value bab_aba​. A detection event occurs when that parity differs from its reference Stim: a fast stabilizer circuit simulator, PDF p. 15 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.22331/q-2021-07-06-497. Write the test as a bit, so that zero means agreement:

Da=⨁j∈Ramj⊕ba,Di,t=si,t⊕si,t−1for a repeated check.D_a=\bigoplus_{j\in R_a}m_j\oplus b_a, \qquad D_{i,t}=s_{i,t}\oplus s_{i,t-1}\quad\text{for a repeated check}.Da​=j∈Ra​⨁​mj​⊕ba​,Di,t​=si,t​⊕si,t−1​for a repeated check.
(4.5)Definition

The second form is Module 1's syndrome difference. A persistent data error changes later reports sss, but only its arrival changes their difference. Differencing removes the persistent baseline; the pattern in space and time still carries information about the cause.

The ends of the experiment need different comparisons. A temporal endcap uses known preparation information or final data readout to close the record. Let bib_ibi​ be a known initial check parity, TTT the number of measured rounds, and zqz_qzq​ a final Z-basis data result. For checks compatible with that preparation and readout,

Di,1=si,1⊕bi,Di,T+1=si,T⊕⨁q∈supp⁡Sizq(Si a Z check).\begin{aligned} D_{i,1}&=s_{i,1}\oplus b_i,\\ D_{i,T+1}&=s_{i,T}\oplus\bigoplus_{q\in\operatorname{supp}S_i}z_q \qquad(S_i\text{ a Z check}). \end{aligned}Di,1​Di,T+1​​=si,1​⊕bi​,=si,T​⊕q∈suppSi​⨁​zq​(Si​ a Z check).​
(4.6)
Derivation · Close the record with known parities

Use the product of individual Z eigenvalues to recover a Z-check eigenvalue. A noiseless first measurement of a known check returns (−1)si,1=(−1)bi(-1)^{s_{i,1}}=(-1)^{b_i}(−1)si,1​=(−1)bi​, giving the first comparison. At destructive Z readout,

∏q∈supp⁡Si(−1)zq=(−1)⨁qzq.\prod_{q\in\operatorname{supp}S_i}(-1)^{z_q} =(-1)^{\bigoplus_q z_q}.q∈suppSi​∏​(−1)zq​=(−1)⨁q​zq​.

Without intervening faults this sign equals (−1)si,T(-1)^{s_{i,T}}(−1)si,T​, giving the final comparison. The product state ∣0⟩⊗9|0\rangle^{\otimes9}∣0⟩⊗9 fixes the Z checks but is not an eigenstate of an X check. Its first X-check signs are random. Later X outcomes repeat those signs, so bulk differences remain predictable. Final Z data results supply no X parity. Preparing and reading in X swaps the roles of the families. The endcaps follow the available eigenvalue information Quantum error correction for quantum memories, PDF p. 30 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.87.307.

A negative first result

Prepare all nine data qubits in ∣0⟩|0\rangle∣0⟩. All four Z checks start positive. Suppose the first X-a result is 111 and the next is also 111. Their bulk detector is 1⊕1=01\oplus1=01⊕1=0. There is no first-round X-a detector comparing its result to zero. At the end, the nine Z readouts close all four Z checks, including the weight-two boundary checks, but no X check.

Is the first sign an error?

An X check is negative in the first round of ∣0⟩⊗9|0\rangle^{\otimes9}∣0⟩⊗9 preparation. Is that alone evidence of an error?

Your answer

Google's ZXXZ circuit uses local Hadamards to choose its preparation and readout basis. Undo the local basis map from Module 3 before assigning CSS endcaps. Its final data results close only the compatible checks Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 25 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y.

Now inject an elementary Pauli fault and propagate it to every measurement it flips. The resulting set of flipped detectors is its fault signature. Also track whether it flips the reported logical observable. Such a logical-observable flip changes the parity we intend to preserve; it need not create a detector event.

A detector error model, using Stim's documentation terminology, lists fault probabilities, detector sets and logical-observable flips. The honeycomb-memory paper calls the detector sets symptoms and the logical flips frame changes A Fault-Tolerant Honeycomb Memory, PDF pp. 5-6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.22331/q-2021-12-20-605. Stim groups circuit faults by these effects Stim: a fast stabilizer circuit simulator, PDF p. 13 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.22331/q-2021-07-06-497. Google uses such models when preparing its decoder training data Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 13 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. Let fjf_jfj​ indicate fault jjj, let column jjj of AAA contain its detector signature, and let ℓj\ell_jℓj​ be its logical-flip bit:

D=Af(mod2),L=ℓ⋅f(mod2),entry j=(pj,{a:Aaj=1},ℓj).D=Af\pmod2,\qquad L=\ell\cdot f\pmod2, \qquad\text{entry }j=(p_j,\{a:A_{aj}=1\},\ell_j).D=Af(mod2),L=ℓ⋅f(mod2),entry j=(pj​,{a:Aaj​=1},ℓj​).
(4.7)Definition

XOR adds Pauli signatures, including cancellation at shared endpoints. Treating the entries as independent random events is a separate assumption. Mutually exclusive alternatives at one gate and persistent leakage need additional care.

A signature with two detector endpoints is a graph edge. One with a single endpoint can be represented by an edge to a virtual boundary, where no second detector is measured. A hyperedge joins more than two detector endpoints.

For Y5Y_5Y5​, those four checks are distinct. A boundary Y can have fewer endpoints. Even independent Pauli noise can correlate X and Z components through its Y alternative. Independent locations do not imply independent component decoders Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 16 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y.

How many checks change?

A Y5Y_5Y5​ arrives between ideal interior rounds on our patch. How many checks change?

Explanation

Four: X-a and X-b see its Z component; Z-a and Z-b see its X component.

The signature description makes circuit distance precise. Let ∣f∣|f|∣f∣ count elementary fault locations, restricting the minimum to combinations allowed by the circuit's noise model:

dcirc=min⁡{ ∣f∣:Af=0, ℓ⋅f=1 }.d_{\rm circ}=\min\{\,|f|:Af=0,\ \ell\cdot f=1\,\}.dcirc​=min{∣f∣:Af=0, ℓ⋅f=1}.
(4.8)Definition

Two allowed histories with the same detector record can demand different logical corrections. Their difference is an undetected logical history when that difference is allowed. This explains why a decoder can fail before dcircd_{\rm circ}dcirc​ faults occur. Module 5 will choose between such histories using their probabilities.

Time supplies another direction for an error chain. If both temporal ends are unconstrained, a short interval can be crossed by few wrong reports. Fault-tolerant parity measurements therefore commonly use order-ddd rounds when measurement and data faults are comparable Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation, PDF p. 13 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.86.032324. A decoding window is the portion of history retained while older inferences are settled; its length must respect these correlations Topological quantum memory, PDF pp. 22-23 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754. A product-prepared memory with destructive readout has basis-dependent endcaps. Its distance is not universally min⁡(d,T)\min(d,T)min(d,T).

  • Open repetition chain with checks Si=ZiZi+1S_i=Z_iZ_{i+1}Si​=Zi​Zi+1​. Data start in the all-zero word, no correction pulses occur, and final data readout is perfect.

Initial conditions
The cumulative error bits start at eq,0=0e_{q,0}=0eq,0​=0, with known check parities bi=0b_i=0bi​=0. Every control change starts a new record.
Boundary conditions
The chain has open spatial ends, represented by left and right virtual boundaries. The first detector compares a report with its known initial parity. The last compares the final check report with the parity of perfect data readout. There is no periodic boundary. Surface-code time boundaries depend on the preparation and readout basis; this board contains only Z checks.
Reports, differences and compatible fault edges
Two aligned grids show recorded parities and detector bits. The reference row contains known initial parities; row T+1 contains final data parities. Individual final data bits appear below the grids. Muted edges show every allowed single data or report fault. Highlighted edges mark the injected history, not a decoded explanation. In leakage mode, each changed report has its own temporal edge; an outlined report marks any overwrite, including an unchanged bit. Horizontal: Check i (check index). Vertical: Comparison t, increasing down (rounds).

Discrete points give the number of firing checks divided by d-1 at each comparison. Straight line segments connect the points as a visual guide; comparisons occur only at integer rounds. Vertical: Firing checks / (d-1) (fraction).

Method: Track cumulative Boolean data flips, injecting a data fault before its chosen parity extraction. XOR one selected report for a measurement fault. For the leakage surrogate, visit affected rounds first and touching checks in increasing index. Starting from the seed, xorshift32 applies shifts 13 left, 17 unsigned right and 5 left, retaining 32 bits after each step; its high bit replaces the report. Truthful reports resume after the interval. Append the final data parities and XOR consecutive rows. A data fault at q,t joins checks q-1 and q in row t, with a missing endpoint replaced by a spatial boundary. A report fault at i,t joins that check in rows t and t+1. Count all comparisons with denominator (d-1)(T+1), or bulk comparisons t=2 through T with denominator (d-1)(T-1).

Tolerances: Bits, event counts and reduced fractions use exact integer arithmetic. Decimal fractions agree within 1e-12. Seed 7 gives the first four report bits 0, 0, 1, 1. This is one reproducible record, not a Monte Carlo estimate.

Display conventions

  • Data are rings and Z checks are hollow squares. A data X uses solid crossing strokes. Report-fault edges are dotted; event nodes carry a ring and the bit 1.
  • Time increases downward in both grids and rightward in the trace. A reference row at t=0 is not a detector comparison.
  • Tab to a detector and press Enter or Space, or select it with a pointer, to inspect the two parity bits being compared.
  • Muted graph edges are possible single-fault explanations. There is no matching solver and no inferred correction.
  • Surface-code detection probabilities use a stated set of check types, weights and boundary comparisons. This single repetition record is not that experimental average.

Model limits

The repetition chain protects against X errors only. This lab has no quantum-state amplitudes, gate propagation or decoder.

The leakage surrogate does not predict physical leakage lifetimes, propagation or logical error rates.

Equal event counts can hide different event geometries. The fraction alone does not identify the cause or logical consequence.

The board is capped at seven data bits and ten measured rounds. Only faults before measured rounds are allowed; final data readout is ideal.

Changing the number of rounds demonstrates boundary comparisons. It does not establish a temporal logical distance.

You can now build the detector record, including its time boundaries, and predict which entries a fault flips. A decoder also needs probabilities for those possible faults.

§

4.4 · Noise models: what is allowed to fail?

A physical error probability is meaningful only after we say where a fault can occur and what it does. Different noise models answer different questions about the same code.

A code-capacity model puts noise on data and assumes perfect extraction. A phenomenological model additionally corrupts reports, without building their extraction gates. A circuit-level model places faults at gates, idle intervals, preparation and measurement. It can therefore produce hooks and record errors from the same cause Quantum error correction for quantum memories, PDF pp. 18,28 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.87.307.

Our depolarizing channel applies a uniformly chosen nonidentity Pauli with total probability ppp. For nnn qubits, let Pn\mathcal P_nPn​ contain the tensor products of I,X,Y,ZI,X,Y,ZI,X,Y,Z without overall phases:

Dn,p(ρ)=(1−p)ρ+p4n−1∑P∈Pn∖{I}PρP.\mathcal D_{n,p}(\rho)=(1-p)\rho+ \frac{p}{4^n-1}\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_n\setminus\{I\}}P\rho P.Dn,p​(ρ)=(1−p)ρ+4n−1p​P∈Pn​∖{I}∑​PρP.
(4.11)Definition

Here ppp is not the probability of replacing the state by the maximally mixed state. A report flips with probability qqq; a reset prepares the wrong computational state with probability rrr. Model a report error as a flip of the classical recorded bit. Model a reset error as preparation of the wrong computational state.

One fault location, several alternatives

A one-qubit depolarizing location has three nonidentity alternatives, each with probability p/3p/3p/3. A two-qubit location has 42−1=154^2-1=1542−1=15, each with probability p/15p/15p/15 Low-distance Surface Codes under Realistic Quantum Noise, PDF p. 8 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062320. A CNOT fault may act on both data and ancilla. Its ancilla part can reach later data gates. A classical report flip changes the record but cannot propagate backward into the data.

One possible uniform circuit recipe uses Dn,p\mathcal D_{n,p}Dn,p​ after every gate, D1,p\mathcal D_{1,p}D1,p​ for every idle layer, wrong reset with probability ppp, and wrong report with probability ppp. The word “circuit-level” alone does not specify that recipe.

Model What fails and what its parameter means Correlations retained or omitted
Code capacity Data channel with probability ppp; extraction ideal No faults in the extraction circuit
Phenomenological Data channel ppp, independent report flips qqq per round Time ambiguity, without gate propagation
Uniform circuit recipe Gates, idles, reset and reports as specified here Propagation of local faults; no persistent leakage
SD6 CNOT and one-qubit gates at ppp; reset, readout and idle at ppp Source-defined standard depolarizing circuit
SI1000 CZ at ppp; one-qubit gates and idle at p/10p/10p/10; reset at 2p2p2p; readout at 5p5p5p Additional idle depolarization 2p2p2p during others' measurement or reset
Pauli+ Calibrated component channels, with leakage and unwanted interactions Physics beyond a Pauli-only circuit simulation

SD6 and SI1000 are named recipes in the honeycomb-memory comparison, also applied there to surface codes. Their reset error is X after preparing zero; their readout error is X before Z measurement. The additional SI1000 idle channel can stack with its ordinary idle channel A Fault-Tolerant Honeycomb Memory, PDF pp. 4-5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.22331/q-2021-12-20-605. Their names do not prescribe the number of layers in our surface-code schedule. Google's Pauli+ adds calibrated leakage and crosstalk processes to a Pauli simulation; it is not a synonym for every circuit-level model Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit, PDF p. 21 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-022-05434-1.

Does the same p mean the same hardware?

One paper uses ideal measurements; another faults every CNOT. Can their thresholds be compared as hardware quality?

Optional. A Pauli mixture discards relative phases between error amplitudes. Pauli twirling averages a channel over Pauli conjugations Low-distance Surface Codes under Realistic Quantum Noise, PDF p. 6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062320. For a coherent rotation RX(θ)R_X(\theta)RX​(θ), its twirled channel is

Derivation · Cancel the cross terms

Expand RX=cI−isXR_X=cI-isXRX​=cI−isX, with c=cos⁡(θ/2)c=\cos(\theta/2)c=cos(θ/2) and s=sin⁡(θ/2)s=\sin(\theta/2)s=sin(θ/2):

RXρRX†=c2ρ+s2XρX+ics(ρX−Xρ).R_X\rho R_X^\dagger=c^2\rho+s^2X\rho X+ics(\rho X-X\rho).RX​ρRX†​=c2ρ+s2XρX+ics(ρX−Xρ).

Conjugating the channel by Z changes XXX to −X-X−X. The cross term changes sign; the diagonal terms remain. I and X give one sign, Y and Z the other, so averaging cancels the cross terms. The same sign orthogonality removes unequal-Pauli terms in a general channel expansion. Replacing a physical channel by this average is an approximation unless a suitable randomization protocol implements it.

Module 2's coherent-rotation exercise shows why the discarded phases can matter over repeated operations.

You can now state what a noise parameter means and what a simulation leaves out. Leakage is a particularly important way for a transmon to leave the Pauli model.

§

4.5 · Leakage, bursts and the floor

A transmon can leave the two levels that encode its bit. If that population survives, the same qubit can disturb several later rounds.

The computational subspace is span⁡{∣0⟩,∣1⟩}\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle\}span{∣0⟩,∣1⟩}. Leakage is population outside it, for example in ∣2⟩|2\rangle∣2⟩. A Pauli changes a state within the computational subspace. A leaked transmon instead presents a different input to its next gate. That gate can impart an unwanted phase to a neighbor or transport leakage through higher-level resonances Overcoming leakage in quantum error correction, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41567-023-02226-w. One leakage event can therefore disturb several checks across several rounds.

Multilevel reset returns a measure qubit to the ground state even when it occupies higher excited levels. One implementation sweeps its excitations into the readout resonator, lets them decay, and returns the qubit to its operating frequency Removing leakage-induced correlated errors in superconducting quantum error correction, PDF p. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41467-021-21982-y. This also erases its computational state, which is acceptable after readout.

Data carry the unknown logical amplitudes. Data-qubit leakage removal, or DQLR, must preserve valid computational states while extracting unwanted population. In Miao and colleagues' protocol, measure-qubit reset is followed by a selective interaction that transports data leakage to the measure qubit, then another measure-qubit reset Overcoming leakage in quantum error correction, PDF p. 3 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41567-023-02226-w. The operation returns leaked data to the computational subspace; it does not reconstruct logical information already lost to leakage.

Why not reset all the data?

Why not remove data leakage by resetting every data qubit?

Your answer

Revisit the detector board. Its leakage setting replaces reports of checks touching the selected site with independent fair bits for leak_length rounds. The true data remain unchanged. seed fixes a reproducible realization. This is a surrogate for persistent untrusted reports, not a transmon channel or a prediction of leakage lifetime and spread.

Is the average enough?

Would equal average event fractions imply equal logical error rates?

A decoder responds to patterns and their probabilities. The average discards where events occurred and how long their cause persisted.

Your prediction

Use . Seed 777 overwrites S1 and S2 with 000000 in round 333, then 111111 in round 444. Both checks fire in rounds 444 and 555 as those reports change and return to truth. The true final data are 000000000. The all-comparison fraction is 4/14=2/74/14=2/74/14=2/7; the bulk fraction is 4/10=0.44/10=0.44/10=0.4. Compare , whose single corrupted report has a shorter signature.

In Google's 72-qubit surface-code experiment, the average detection probability rises during operation without DQLR. With DQLR that rise disappears Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 25, Fig. S11 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. The important change also includes shorter correlations: a surviving leaked state can disturb later cycles Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF p. 18 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. An average alone cannot capture that history.

A correlated burst is a disturbance that raises fault rates together across a region or interval. High-energy impacts provide one mechanism. Energy deposited in the substrate creates phonons, which can break Cooper pairs. The resulting quasiparticles can absorb qubit energy while tunneling through a junction, producing correlated relaxation Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41567-021-01432-8. Engineering different superconducting gaps on the junction's two sides can obstruct that tunneling channel Resisting high-energy impact events through gap engineering in superconducting qubit arrays, PDF p. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.240601.

Google's 72-qubit repetition experiments attribute mitigation of earlier impact failures to gap engineering, but find newer rare bursts whose cause remains unsettled Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF pp. 4-5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. Their high-distance results, decoded by minimum-weight perfect matching, approach an apparent floor near 10−1010^{-10}10−10 logical errors per cycle. At d=29d=29d=29 they observe zero logical errors; a finite zero-error sample does not establish zero probability Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF pp. 4-5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. Module 1's floor model captures how a separate failure process can limit suppression. Its independent-union assumption does not describe every burst mechanism.

Tangent: where the syndrome information goes

Optional. Recovery can move error information into an ancilla and its environment while preserving the logical amplitudes. For a correctable error set, the recovered data factor from a syndrome register; resetting that register exports its information through a dissipative process Quantum Information, Chapter 7: Quantum Error Correction (Ph219/CS219 lecture notes, updated March 2026), PDF pp. 14-15 Original source ↗. This is the correctability condition developed in Module 2. A measure qubit is a temporary register, not itself a cold bath. Reset alone does not prove that arbitrary data-environment entanglement has been undone. Return to the physical CZ gate to see one route into leakage.

You can now distinguish a single Pauli event from a disturbance that persists across rounds. The physical gate explains one route into those unwanted levels.

§

4.6 · The device behind the circuit

The same interaction that gives a two-qubit gate its conditional phase can populate an unwanted level. The pulse must control both the phase and the return of population.

Transmons are weakly anharmonic oscillators. The pair state ∣11⟩|11\rangle∣11⟩ has one excitation on each transmon; ∣02⟩|02\rangle∣02⟩ has both on the second. Tuning their energies toward resonance lets an interaction mix them. Their hybridized energies repel at an avoided crossing. These are states of the two data or measure transmons, not excited states of the coupler.

Flux controls qubit and coupler frequencies. A tunable coupler changes the effective interaction by balancing direct and coupler-mediated exchange A tunable coupling scheme for implementing high-fidelity two-qubit gates, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevApplied.10.054062. Sycamore uses this principle to suppress exchange at idle and activate it for gates Supplementary information for "Quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor", PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-019-1666-5. Small exchange does not guarantee that every residual conditional interaction vanishes. During a CZ pulse, both the qubit frequency path and the coupling matter Optimizing quantum gates towards the scale of logical qubits, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-46623-y.

Keep only ∣00⟩,∣11⟩,∣02⟩|00\rangle,|11\rangle,|02\rangle∣00⟩,∣11⟩,∣02⟩ to isolate the return-and-phase mechanism. The detuning Δ=ω02−ω11\Delta=\omega_{02}-\omega_{11}Δ=ω02​−ω11​ and real positive effective coupling matrix element ggg are angular frequencies. Use a rotating frame and local Z compensation that remove the computational single-qubit phases. Our rectangular pulse holds g,Δg,\Deltag,Δ constant, with coupling zero outside the pulse:

Method: Evaluate the two-state block exponential, retaining its common factor e−iΔt/2e^{-i\Delta t/2}e−iΔt/2. The spectator amplitude stays fixed. Model limits

Three retained states and one coupled leakage channel. The model omits ∣20⟩|20\rangle∣20⟩, coupler excitation, higher levels, drive distortion, dissipation, crosstalk and pulse ramps.

A resonant full excursion produces π\piπ here. Experimental high-fidelity CZ design cannot be read off a duration slider.

Coherent leakage population is distinct from the stochastic gate-error probabilities in Table S4.

The controls cover detunings from -100 to 100 MHz and durations up to 100 ns, with 201 time samples for prompt interaction. These are teaching-model ranges, not device operating limits.

A complete correction cycle includes much more than its entangling pulse. Data keep relaxing and dephasing while measure qubits are read and reset; leakage removal adds its own operations.

A TLS, or two-level-system defect, is a microscopic parasitic degree of freedom that can resonantly absorb qubit energy. Its drifting resonance can change a qubit's relaxation rate Fluctuations of Energy-Relaxation Times in Superconducting Qubits, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.090502. Frequency selection therefore balances relaxation hotspots, flux-sensitive dephasing, unwanted interactions and pulse distortion Optimizing quantum gates towards the scale of logical qubits, PDF p. 2 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-46623-y. The resulting circuit performance matters alongside isolated gate quality.

Streaming throughput is the sustained rate at which the decoder accepts and processes records. End-of-shot decoder latency is the delay from receiving the final syndrome to returning a correction. Google's 72-qubit real-time experiment runs cycles of 1.1 μs1.1\,\mu\mathrm s1.1μs and reports latency 63±17 μs63\pm17\,\mu\mathrm s63±17μs for its distance-five memory Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF pp. 5-6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. That latency excludes logical feedback.

Fast rounds, delayed answer

How can a 636363-microsecond decoder latency coexist with 1.11.11.1-microsecond rounds on that 72-qubit processor?

Your answer

You can now calculate phase and leakage in a stated gate model and identify the errors that accumulate elsewhere in the cycle. We can use those mechanisms to read an experimental logical decay and its budget.

4.7 · Sycamore to Willow

A memory experiment tests whether the decoded final value agrees with the prepared value. Repeating that test for several durations separates accumulated failure from error per round.

Prepare a logical eigenstate, run syndrome extraction, then measure the data in the same logical basis. The decoder uses the detector record to predict whether the final logical parity should be flipped. Compare that corrected parity with the prepared value. Repeating the shot estimates accumulated logical failure, Pfail(n)P_{\rm fail}(n)Pfail​(n), after nnn rounds. This probability includes the decoder's choices Exponential suppression of bit or phase errors with cyclic error correction, PDF p. 4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03588-y.

Why not divide it by nnn? A later logical flip can undo an earlier one. Suppose each round flips the logical value independently with the same probability ε\varepsilonε. A previously correct shot becomes wrong with probability ε\varepsilonε; a previously wrong shot remains wrong with probability 1−ε1-\varepsilon1−ε. The imbalance between correct and wrong shots is logical contrast, FL=1−2PfailF_L=1-2P_{\rm fail}FL​=1−2Pfail​. Its initial value C=FL(0)C=F_L(0)C=FL​(0) includes a duration-independent preparation/readout offset in this model:

Pfail(n+1)=ε+(1−2ε)Pfail(n),FL(n)=C(1−2ε)n,Pfail(n)=1−C(1−2ε)n2.\begin{aligned} P_{\rm fail}(n+1)&=\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)P_{\rm fail}(n),\\ F_L(n)&=C(1-2\varepsilon)^n,\\ P_{\rm fail}(n)&=\frac{1-C(1-2\varepsilon)^n}{2}. \end{aligned}Pfail​(n+1)FL​(n)Pfail​(n)​=ε+(1−2ε)Pfail​(n),=C(1−2ε)n,=21−C(1−2ε)n​.​

Derivation · Follow correct and wrong shots separately

Add the mutually exclusive routes to a wrong final value. Write Pn=Pfail(n)P_n=P_{\rm fail}(n)Pn​=Pfail​(n):

Pn+1=ε(1−Pn)⏟correct, then flips+(1−ε)Pn⏟wrong, then stays=ε+(1−2ε)Pn.P_{n+1}=\underbrace{\varepsilon(1-P_n)}_{\text{correct, then flips}} +\underbrace{(1-\varepsilon)P_n}_{\text{wrong, then stays}} =\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)P_n.Pn+1​=correct, then flipsε(1−Pn​)​​+wrong, then stays(1−ε)Pn​​​=ε+(1−2ε)Pn​.

Subtract twice this recurrence from one:

1−2Pn+1=(1−2ε)(1−2Pn),FL(n)=(1−2ε)nFL(0).1-2P_{n+1}=(1-2\varepsilon)(1-2P_n),\qquad F_L(n)=(1-2\varepsilon)^nF_L(0).1−2Pn+1​=(1−2ε)(1−2Pn​),FL​(n)=(1−2ε)nFL​(0).

The intercept C=FL(0)C=F_L(0)C=FL​(0) absorbs a duration-independent preparation/readout contrast loss in the fit. Equivalently, independent input and output sign errors multiply the ideal contrast by their fixed mean signs. The per-round process is stationary and symmetric between the two logical values. At ε=0\varepsilon=0ε=0 the contrast stays CCC; for 0<ε<1/20<\varepsilon<1/20<ε<1/2, it decays to zero and failure approaches 1/21/21/2. This recurrence is the reduced fit model used in the surface-memory analysis Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit, PDF p. 21 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-022-05434-1. A successful fit summarizes the data; it does not establish independence of the underlying physical faults.

Google calls FLF_LFL​ “logical fidelity.” Here it measures the bias of a binary memory result, not the state overlap ⟨ψ∣ρ∣ψ⟩\langle\psi|\rho|\psi\rangle⟨ψ∣ρ∣ψ⟩. Its zero means an equal chance of a correct or wrong logical bit. Taking the logarithm turns exponential contrast decay into a line. Its intercept records CCC; its slope records ε\varepsilonε:

m=dln⁡FLdn=ln⁡(1−2ε),ε=1−em2,FL(nb)FL(na)=(1−2ε)nb−na.m=\frac{\mathrm d\ln F_L}{\mathrm dn}=\ln(1-2\varepsilon),\qquad \varepsilon=\frac{1-e^m}{2},\qquad \frac{F_L(n_b)}{F_L(n_a)}=(1-2\varepsilon)^{n_b-n_a}.m=dndlnFL​​=ln(1−2ε),ε=21−em​,FL​(na​)FL​(nb​)​=(1−2ε)nb​−na​.

Derivation · Remove the intercept and invert the slope

Tangent: what a fitted uncertainty includes

Optional. The papers fit separate logical bases and patches before combining rates. Finite shot counts create sampling uncertainty; drift can create excess fit residuals. You can now trace the reported logical error from repeated measurements through decoding and a decay fit. Module 5 asks how a decoder chooses among compatible histories and how that choice sets the threshold.

4.8 · Reconstruct and transfer

Rebuild the circuit-to-record argument, then use it on a code and a pulse you have not just followed in the examples. Start from memory; use the figures to check a support only after you have explained how you found it.

The required path is reconstruction, transfer and the decay calculation. The pulse calculation and the two challenges are optional. Keep three questions separate throughout: what the circuit measures, what a physical fault does, and what a decoder concludes. A correct answer to the first does not settle the other two.

Follow a fault from the circuit to the record

Without the lesson open, derive the data operator measured by ancilla-only H-CZ-H on X-a and repair it to measure X parity. Then use the CNOT X circuit, ordered NE, NW, SE, SW. Propagate an ancilla X after its second gate. Explain the detector patterns of the resulting data error and of one wrong check report.

Use these supports rather than reconstructing the patch from memory: X-a {1,2,4,5}\{1,2,4,5\}{1,2,4,5}; X-b {5,6,8,9}\{5,6,8,9\}{5,6,8,9}; X-c {2,3}\{2,3\}{2,3}; X-d {7,8}\{7,8\}{7,8}; Z-a {2,3,5,6}\{2,3,5,6\}{2,3,5,6}; Z-b {4,5,7,8}\{4,5,7,8\}{4,5,7,8}; Z-c {1,4}\{1,4\}{1,4}; Z-d {6,9}\{6,9\}{6,9}. Which first and final detectors exist for ∣0⟩⊗9|0\rangle^{\otimes9}∣0⟩⊗9 preparation and Z data readout? Distinguish an undetected logical fault combination from a decoder choosing the wrong explanation. State a model limit.

Hint

Follow final ZAZ_AZA​ backward to find the measured operator. Follow the injected fault forward to find its damage. The ancilla's known reset sign and the data's known initial check signs play different roles.

Check against the rubric
  • Finds +ZAZ1Z2Z4Z5+Z_AZ_1Z_2Z_4Z_5+ZA​Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​, uses the reset sign and repairs the data observable with data H gates.
  • Propagates the midpoint fault to X4X5X_4X_5X4​X5​ and identifies Z-a and Z-c.
  • Distinguishes a parity change on arrival from the entry/exit pair of a bad report, with a within-round timing caveat.
  • Anchors initial/final detectors only for Z checks, while retaining repeated-round X comparisons.
  • Separates circuit distance from decoder failure count and names an excluded mechanism.
Show model solution

The final H changes the backward readout to XAX_AXA​. Each CZ appends its data Z. The first H restores ZAZ_AZA​, whose reset sign is positive. The ancilla matrix elements are therefore (I±Z1Z2Z4Z5)/2(I\pm Z_1Z_2Z_4Z_5)/2(I±Z1​Z2​Z4​Z5​)/2. Hadamards on every participating data wire before and after the full block conjugate each Z to X.

The CNOT circuit touches data 2,1,5,42,1,5,42,1,5,4. After the second gate, only the interactions with 5 and 4 remain:

XA⟼XAX5⟼XAX4X5.X_A\longmapsto X_AX_5\longmapsto X_AX_4X_5.XA​⟼XA​X5​⟼XA​X4​X5​.

The output H changes the ancilla factor to ZAZ_AZA​, without flipping its readout. Z-a and Z-c each meet the data pair once; Z-b meets it twice. Thus an ideal final data-syndrome snapshot flags Z-a and Z-c. In an ideal repeated-check snapshot, an error arriving before a round changes those parities once and then leaves them changed. A wrong report instead changes on entry and again on return to the true value. For a fault inside simultaneous extraction, propagate through the full schedule to determine which round each comparison fires.

All Z checks initially have eigenvalue +1+1+1 in the all-zero product. First X signs can be random, so they supply references for later comparisons rather than immediate error flags. Final Z data measurements reconstruct every Z-check parity and logical Z. They cannot reconstruct X-check parities.

An undetected logical fault combination satisfies Af=0Af=0Af=0 and ℓ⋅f=1\ell\cdot f=1ℓ⋅f=1. A decoder can fail on a nonzero record by choosing a compatible history in the wrong logical class. Neither the local CNOT trace nor a Pauli-signature model includes a leaked transmon persisting through later rounds.

Transfer to the four-data-qubit code

Browne's code has independent stabilizers XXXXXXXXXXXX and ZZZZZZZZZZZZ on four data qubits Topological Codes and Computation, Problem Sheet 1: Stabilizer codes, PDF p. 2, questions 5-7 Original source ↗. Construct extraction circuits and determine the code-space dimension.

An X fault occurs on the X-check ancilla after it has touched data 1 and 2, with 3 and 4 still to come. Does the final data error have a check syndrome? Is it harmless? Explain why detection of every single data Pauli does not guarantee fault-tolerant extraction. This circuit question extends Browne's exercise.

Hint

Count independent constraints. Then compare X3X4X_3X_4X3​X4​ with the stabilizer group, not only with its check syndrome.

Check against the rubric
  • Gives the correct CNOT directions, or CZ circuits with the required basis gates.
  • Finds two encoded qubits, a four-dimensional code space and distance two.
  • Shows that every weight-one Pauli is detected, while X3X4X_3X_4X3​X4​ has syndrome (0,0)(0,0)(0,0).
  • Identifies that hook as a logical operator outside the stabilizer group and distinguishes detection from correction.
Show model solution

For XXXX, prepare A in ∣0⟩|0\rangle∣0⟩, apply H, use A to control a CNOT onto each data qubit, apply H and measure A in Z. For ZZZZ, let each data qubit control a CNOT targeting a fresh zero ancilla, then measure it in Z. There are four data qubits and two independent generators, so k=4−2=2k=4-2=2k=4−2=2 and the code-space dimension is 22=42^2=422=4.

Every weight-one X anticommutes with ZZZZ. Every weight-one Z anticommutes with XXXX; every Y anticommutes with both. For example, Y1Y_1Y1​ has syndrome (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) in the stated check order. The ancilla fault reaches the remaining data qubits and leaves X3X4X_3X_4X3​X4​. Its intersections with ZZZZ have even size, and it commutes with XXXX. Its syndrome is (0,0)(0,0)(0,0).

The stabilizer group is {I,XXXX,ZZZZ,YYYY}\{I,XXXX,ZZZZ,YYYY\}{I,XXXX,ZZZZ,YYYY} with the positive product sign. X3X4X_3X_4X3​X4​ is not in that group. It is a nontrivial logical operator of weight two. There is no weight-one logical operator, so the code has distance two. One physical fault in this extraction can therefore cause an undetected logical action. The ability to detect a single data Pauli assumes a different error set from the one created by a faulty ancilla. A better extraction needs additional fault information or constrained propagation; distance two alone does not promise correction of an arbitrary unknown-location data error.
